name: General Procrastination Scale
construct: Trait procrastination across everyday tasks such as bills, appointments, shopping and correspondence.
licence: Salford PsyTech questionnaire battery, Copyright restrictions field: "No restrictions." No author licence text appears on the York University PDF.
instructions: People may use the following statements to describe themselves. For each statement, decide whether the statement is uncharacteristic or characteristic of you using the following 5 point scale. Note that the 3 on the scale is Neutral – the statement is neither characteristic nor uncharacteristic of you. In the box to the right of each statement, fill in the number on the 5 point scale that best describes you.

items.text: I often find myself performing tasks that I had intended to do days before.
I often miss concerts, sporting events, or the like because I don't around to buying tickets on time.
items.note: Asterisked in source (differs between student and non-student forms). Source text reads "don't around"; likely a typographical omission of "get". Transcribed as printed.

items.text: When planning a party, I make the necessary arrangements well in advance.
items.note: Asterisked in source (differs between student and non-student forms).

items.text: When it is time to get up in the morning, I most often get right out of bed.
A letter may sit for days after I write it before mailing it.
I generally return phone calls promptly.
Even with jobs that require little else except sitting down and doing them, I find they seldom get done for days.
I usually make decisions as soon as possible.
I generally delay before starting on work I have to do.
When travelling, I usually have to rush in preparing to arrive at the airport or station at the appropriate time.
items.note: Asterisked in source (differs between student and non-student forms).

items.text: When preparing to go out, I am seldom caught having to do something at the last minute.
In preparing for some deadline, I often waste time by doing other things.
If a bill for a small amount comes, I pay it right away.
items.note: Asterisked in source (differs between student and non-student forms).

items.text: I usually return an RVSP request very shortly after receiving the invitation.
items.note: Asterisked in source (differs between student and non-student forms). Source spells "RVSP" as printed.

items.text: I often have a task finished sooner than necessary.
I always seem to end up shopping for birthday or Christmas gifts at the last minute.
I usually buy even an essential item at the last minute.
I usually accomplish all the things I plan to do in a day.
I am continually saying "I'll do it tomorrow".
items.note: Source PDF renders the quotation marks and apostrophe as encoding artefacts ("AI=ll do it tomorrow@"); the intended wording is as given here.

items.text: I usually take care of all the tasks I have to do before I settle down and relax for the evening.

subscales.name: Total
subscales.description: Sum of all 20 items after reverse scoring items 3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 13, 14, 15, 18 and 20.

scoring: Reverse score items 3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 13, 14, 15, 18 and 20 (6 minus raw score) and sum all 20 items for a total of 20 to 100; higher scores indicate greater trait procrastination. Source footer: "Note: Reversed-keyed items: 3,4,6,8,11,13,14,15,18,20" and "Note: * indicates items that differ from student to non-student forms". No clinical cut offs are published.
citation: Lay, C. H. (1986). At last, my research article on procrastination. Journal of Research in Personality, 20(4), 474–495. https://doi.org/10.1016/0092-6566(86)90127-3
transcriptionNote: Transcribed from the York University PDF titled "Procrastination Scale (Lay, 1986)". Items 2, 3, 10, 13 and 14 are asterisked as differing between the student and non-student forms; the PDF does not state which form it reproduces. Item 2 contains an apparent typographical omission ("don't around") that has been kept as printed. Item 19 contains encoding artefacts in the PDF for the quotation marks and apostrophe; the wording given here resolves those artefacts and is the only departure from the printed text.
